description: Asian philosophy is a long and broad period, "beginning" in 6th century BCE China and continuing
throughout Asia to the present day. This course spans the Spring and Autumn Period (722-481 BCE)
and the Warring States Period (403-221 BCE) of ancient China and the Golden Age of Buddhist
philosophy in ancient India (1st century BCE to 7th century CE). In the former we will focus on
the Confucians, the Mohists, and the Daoists. In the latter we will focus on Madhyamaka and
Yogacara. The guiding thread behind this course is the concept of the path. What is the path? How
do we know it? Why should we follow it? How does following it inform our lives and communities?
